Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. 1	"""tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py — per-cell L3-TC conversion gate (owner baseline).
2	
3	The owner baseline directive's per-cell gates for a newly-converted L3-TC cell:
4	  (1) megakernel-vs-fp64 single-step   — the in-kernel optimizer TAIL must match a
5	      reference apply of the SAME canonical update on the SAME TC-reduced grad.
6	  (2) A/A/A determinism                — the production L3-TC step is bit-identical
7	      across 3 runs from the same init (fixed tile ownership + ascending-k/t reduce).
8	
9	RE-ANCHOR (task #10): the eager per-op CUDA kernels are being DELETED, so (1) no longer
10	runs a fresh eager optimizer + opt.step(); the reference is now the PURE-fp64 canonical
11	transcription (ref_<opt>_step in tests/hw/test_reference_parity.py) applied PER TENSOR on
12	the kernel's captured grad + zero-init state. bf16 STAYS the compute precision (the kernel
13	is unchanged); fp64 is only the ground-truth yardstick.
14	
15	WHY THIS SHAPE (not a full loss-trajectory-vs-eager oracle): the bf16 wgmma fwd+bwd
16	and the deterministic grad reduction are SHARED with the already-gated adamw TC cell
17	(decoder 13/13+5, vit 21/21, mamba 5/5 — grad parity vs the bf16-faithful oracle).
18	A converted cell changes ONLY the per-element tail (apply_optimizer<Opt>), which is
19	the 14/0-apply-parity math. So the cell-specific NEW surface is exactly the tail, and
20	the right gate is "did the kernel's tail apply the canonical update to the reduced
21	grad correctly" — which is (1). The grad itself is validated by the adamw gates +
22	the determinism check (2) proves no race was introduced by the tail swap.
23	
24	The reference apply is the canonical fp64 math (transcribed from csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h
25	— the SAME single source the kernel's apply_optimizer<Opt> compiles from), run on the grad
26	the kernel returns (fused_train_step(return_grad=True)). bf16-TC kernel vs fp64 reference →
27	fp32-reorder tol (1e-4); the SAM 2nd-backward surfaces (sharpness/sam_dir) carry the bf16-
28	TC-vs-fp64 floor tol (3e-2 / 2.5e-2).
29	
30	Run:
31	  PYTHONPATH=. python -m tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate                 # all converted
32	  PYTHONPATH=. python -m tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate --cell lion/decoder
33	  PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py -q
34	"""
35	from __future__ import annotations
36	
37	import argparse
38	import os
39	import subprocess
40	import sys
41	from pathlib import Path
42	
43	import torch
44	
45	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
46	
47	# ── CROSS-CELL ISOLATION (test-state-leakage fix, #19d) ───────────────────────
48	# The SuperGrok2 gate's per-op ORACLE (ops.supergrok2_batched_step) and the eager
49	# per-op neuralgrok_fused_step kernel both perturb a device-global (raw-cudaMalloc /
50	# __constant__ scratch) that a SUBSEQUENT TC SuperGrok2 launch reads — so when the

158	    # kSgPhiHidden — the known prior 64-bug). lamb=1.0 (the production supergrok_lamb default).

196	def _neuralgrok_canonical_mv(grad, opt_obj, step, p_before=None):
197	    """The (m, v, p_after) the NeuralGrok tail MUST produce, by the canonical header math.
198	
199	    Transcribes csrc/algorithms/neuralgrok.h (the SINGLE source the kernel's
200	    apply_optimizer<NeuralGrok> calls) — the gate's docstring defines its reference as
201	    exactly this header math:
202	        psi   = sum_j psi_W2[j] * relu(psi_W1[j]*|g| + psi_b1[j]) + psi_b2   (kPsiHidden=16)
203	        g_amp = (psi*alpha + beta) * g
204	        m     = beta1*m_prev + (1-beta1)*g_amp        (m_prev = 0 at step 1, zero-init cache)
205	        v     = beta2*v_prev + (1-beta2)*g_amp^2
206	        update= (m/bc1) / (sqrt(v/bc2) + eps);  p_after = p - lr*(update + wd*p)   (AdamW tail)
207	    computed in fp64 on the SAME captured TC-reduced grad and the SAME psi weights the
208	    kernel read (opt_obj.psi_pack). Returns flat fp32 (m, v, p_after) for the whole param
209	    vector; p_after is None when p_before is None (the (1b)-only call shape).
210	
211	    RE-ANCHOR (task #10): the eager per-op neuralgrok_fused_step CUDA kernel is being
212	    DELETED, so BOTH (1a) params and (1b) m/v are now anchored to THIS ground-truth fp64
213	    transcription of neuralgrok.h — the same single source the kernel's apply_optimizer<
214	    NeuralGrok> compiles from. The kernel matches this canonical math to ~2.7e-7. (1a) used
215	    to compare the live eager opt.step(); with the eager path gone, the AdamW tail here IS
216	    the (1a) reference. bf16 stays the compute precision; fp64 is the yardstick.
217	    """
218	    dev = grad.device
219	    g64 = grad.double()
220	    # GLOBAL grad-norm clip — neuralgrok.h's tail clips the reduced grad (kernel P2.5,
221	    # st.clip_coef) BEFORE psi+amp. Apply the SAME clip to the reference so it tracks the
222	    # kernel when the clip FIRES (global grad-norm > grad_clip, e.g. seed 7); inert
223	    # (coef=1) when norm<=clip. total_norm = sqrt(Σ g²) over the reduced grad == the
224	    # kernel's P2.5 norm.
225	    _gclip = float(opt_obj.param_groups[0].get("grad_clip", 0.0))
226	    if _gclip > 0.0:
227	        _tn = g64.norm().item()
228	        if _tn > _gclip:
229	            g64 = g64 * (_gclip / (_tn + 1e-6))
230	    ag = g64.abs()
231	    pack = opt_obj.psi_pack(device=dev).double()
232	    H = (pack.numel() - 1) // 3
233	    W1 = pack[0:H]; b1 = pack[H:2 * H]; W2 = pack[2 * H:3 * H]; b2 = pack[3 * H]
234	    # psi = sum_j W2[j]*relu(W1[j]*|g| + b1[j]) + b2  (per element)
235	    hid = torch.relu(ag.unsqueeze(1) * W1.reshape(1, H) + b1.reshape(1, H))   # [N,H]
236	    psi = (hid * W2.reshape(1, H)).sum(1) + b2                                # [N]
237	    grp = opt_obj.param_groups[0]
238	    alpha = float(grp["alpha"]); beta = float(grp["beta"])
239	    beta1, beta2 = float(grp["betas"][0]), float(grp["betas"][1])
240	    g_amp = (psi * alpha + beta) * g64
241	    # step 1 from zero-init moments (the kernel's state cache zero-inits [m|v|extra]).
242	    m = (1.0 - beta1) * g_amp
243	    v = (1.0 - beta2) * g_amp * g_amp
244	    p_after = None
245	    if p_before is not None:
246	        # AdamW tail (the (1a) reference). bc1=1-β1, bc2=1-β2 at t=1.
247	        lr = float(grp.get("lr", 1e-3)); eps = float(grp.get("eps", 1e-8))
248	        wd = float(grp.get("weight_decay", 0.0))
249	        bc1 = 1.0 - beta1; bc2 = 1.0 - beta2
250	        pb = p_before.double().to(dev)
251	        update = (m / bc1) / (torch.sqrt(v / bc2) + eps)
252	        p_after = (pb - lr * (update + wd * pb)).float()
253	    return m.float(), v.float(), p_after

256	def _neuralgrok_factory(g, params, c):
257	    # train_neuralgrok: NeuralGrok(lr, betas, weight_decay, alpha=neural_alpha,
258	    #                              beta=neural_beta, num_layers=neural_layers,
259	    #                              hidden_dim=neural_hidden, grad_clip=neural_grad_clip).
260	    # PARITY PINS (the kernel's compile-time psi contract — OPTIMIZER_CONFIGS sets
261	    # these too): num_layers=2 and hidden_dim=16 == kPsiHidden, so the trained MLP IS
262	    # the deployed MLP (psi_pack maps it 1:1 into the kernel's `extra` slice). grad_clip
263	    # is forwarded from the config (default 1.0, == train_neuralgrok); the kernel's P2.5
264	    # clip applies it, and the canonical fp64 reference (_neuralgrok_canonical_mv) applies
265	    # the SAME clip — so the parity is real at any seed (inert when ‖g‖₂≤grad_clip).
266	    params = list(params)
267	    opt = g.NeuralGrok(params, lr=c["lr"], betas=(c["beta1"], c["beta2"]),
268	                       weight_decay=c["weight_decay"],
269	                       alpha=c.get("neural_alpha", 10.0),
270	                       beta=c.get("neural_beta", 4.0),
271	                       num_layers=c.get("neural_layers", 2),
272	                       hidden_dim=c.get("neural_hidden", 16),
273	                       grad_clip=c.get("neural_grad_clip", 1.0))
274	    # The amplifier is constructed on CPU in __init__; the race moves it to the
275	    # param device (grokking_race_v2.py:1094 opt.amplifier=opt.amplifier.to(dev)).
276	    # Mirror that — without it get_weights()/psi_pack() return CPU tensors, and the
277	    # kernel reads the psi `extra` slice from the wrong device. This is the production
278	    # device placement, not a test crutch.
279	    if params:
280	        opt.amplifier = opt.amplifier.to(params[0].device)
281	    return opt

551	def _build_cell(model, seed=int(os.environ.get("GATE_SEED", "42"))):
552	    """Build the live race model + one real batch + the L3-REAL flat layout.
553	
554	    DETERMINISM (load-bearing for gate 2): build_model does NOT reseed from
555	    c["seed"] internally — it draws from the global RNG — so the A/A/A determinism
556	    check MUST reseed here, or each rebuild yields different random init weights and
557	    the gate would compare runs with DIFFERENT inputs (a test bug, not kernel
558	    non-determinism). We torch.manual_seed(seed) immediately before build_model so
559	    every _build_cell(model, seed) returns byte-identical initial params."""
560	    g = _g()
561	    c = dict(g.DEFAULT_CONFIG)
562	    c.update({"model_type": model, "use_amp": False, "use_fused": True,
563	              "compile_model": False, "matmul_precision": "bf16", "seed": seed,
564	              "frac_train": 0.5, "val_ratio": 0.10, "p": 97})
565	    dev = torch.device("cuda")
566	    data = tuple(d.to(dev) for d in g.make_data_for_task(c, seed))
567	    torch.manual_seed(seed)            # pin build_model's global-RNG draw
568	    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)
569	    m = g.build_model(c, dev)
570	    return g, c, m, data, dev

573	def _sg_bf16_sharpness_oracle(model, named_ref, tx, ty, grad, rho, total, dev):
574	    """The (g_sam − g)² sharpness the SAM 2nd backward MUST produce, via the bf16-FAITHFUL
575	    fp64 oracle (the SAME instrument the looksam sam_dir check + the first-grad gate use).
576	    Runs the oracle TWICE — at p and at p'=p+ron·g (ron=rho/‖g‖_global, g the kernel's reduced
577	    grad) — and returns sharpness_bf = (g_sam_bf − g_bf)² flattened (named layout order). The
578	    bf16-TC kernel 2nd backward vs this fp64-bf16-faithful 2nd backward differ only by the bf16
579	    floor (the SAME design floor the looksam sam_dir 2e-2 tol calibrates), so sharpness is
580	    checked at that floor. A SKIPPED SAM phase (sharpness≈0) fails the liveness assert."""
581	    if model == "decoder":
582	        from tests.hw.test_decoder_tc import _bf16_faithful_oracle as _orc
583	        B = int(tx.shape[0]); B16 = B - (B % 16)
584	        a0 = tx[:B16].to(torch.long); a1 = ty[:B16].to(torch.long)
585	        named_d = {n: p.detach() for n, p in named_ref}
586	        _lo, go = _orc(named_d, a0, a1)
587	    elif model == "mamba":
588	        # The mamba twin of the decoder branch: int tokens, the bf16-faithful fp64 mamba
589	        # oracle (the SAME instrument the looksam/mamba sam_dir check + the first-grad gate
590	        # use). B%16 truncation matches fused_train_step's wgmma path.
591	        from tests.hw.test_mamba_tc import _bf16_faithful_mamba_oracle as _orc
592	        B = int(tx.shape[0]); B16 = B - (B % 16)
593	        a0 = tx[:B16].to(torch.long); a1 = ty[:B16].to(torch.long)
594	        named_d = {n: p.detach() for n, p in named_ref}
595	        _lo, go = _orc(named_d, a0, a1)
596	    elif model == "vit":
597	        from tests.hw.test_vit_tc import _bf16_faithful_oracle as _orc
598	        B = int(tx.shape[0]); B16 = B - (B % 16)
599	        a0 = tx[:B16].detach().cpu().double(); a1 = ty[:B16].detach().cpu().to(torch.long)
600	        named_d = {n: p.detach().cpu() for n, p in named_ref}
601	        _lo, go = _orc(named_d, a0, a1)
602	    else:
603	        raise NotImplementedError(f"sg sharpness oracle not wired for {model}")
604	    gn = torch.sqrt(sum((gv.double() ** 2).sum() for gv in go.values())).item()
605	    ron = rho / gn
606	    off = 0; named_pert = {}
607	    cpu = (model == "vit")
608	    for n_, p in named_ref:
609	        k = p.numel()
610	        base = (p.detach().cpu().double() if cpu else p.detach().double())
611	        gslice = grad[off:off + k].reshape(p.shape)
612	        gslice = (gslice.cpu().double() if cpu else gslice.double())
613	        named_pert[n_] = base + ron * gslice
614	        off += k
615	    _lo2, go2 = _orc(named_pert, a0, a1)
616	    sharp = torch.cat([((go2[n_] - go[n_]).reshape(-1).double()) ** 2
617	                       for n_, _ in named_ref]).float().to(dev)
618	    return sharp

882	def run_sg11_warmup_gate(cell_key, warmup_steps=2, verbose=True):
883	    """WARM-UP SG11 gate — the divergence-exercising check the cold single-step gate is
884	    BLIND to (in the worst case mu≈0 ∧ momentum=0 at step 1 ⇒ cos(grad,mu)==cos(grad,
885	    momentum)==gate(0.5) — the two formulations COINCIDE). After ≥1 warm-up step BOTH
886	    mu≠0 AND momentum (exp_avg)≠0, so the BUGGY cos(grad,mu) gate and the CANONICAL
887	    cos(grad,momentum) gate genuinely differ.
888	
889	    Runs `warmup_steps` real L3-TC steps (shared state_cache so exp_avg accumulates),
890	    captures the start-of-step m/v/p going INTO the gated step (= the kernel's
891	    st.exp_avg/exp_avg_sq/params at gate time), then runs the gated step and validates
892	    the kernel vs the CORRECTED cos(grad,momentum) reference (_run_sg_cell_gate with
893	    sg11_warmup_state). Returns (ok, detail). detail carries:
894	      * gate_div — max |gate_momentum − gate_mu| over tensors (>0 proves the warm-up
895	        exercises the divergence the bug lives in; the OLD kernel computes the gate_mu
896	        column and must FAIL this corrected reference).
897	      * mom_norm — the start-of-step momentum L2 norm (must be ≫0 — a live warm-up)."""
898	    import math
899	    from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import (has_l3_real, gemm_impl_for_cell,
900	                                              canonicalize_model, fused_train_step,
901	                                              _opt_scalars_from)
902	    spec = _CELLS[cell_key]
903	    model, opt = spec["model"], spec["opt"]
904	    assert opt == "supergrok11", f"{cell_key}: warmup gate is SG11-only"
905	    g, c, m, data, dev = _build_cell(model)
906	    canon = canonicalize_model(model)
907	    assert has_l3_real(canon, opt), f"{cell_key}: not L3-REAL"
908	    assert gemm_impl_for_cell(canon, opt, "bf16") == "wgmma", f"{cell_key}: not wgmma"
909	    tx, ty = data[0], data[1]
910	    # Build the live optimizer with a LARGE meta-net rescale so the gate-dependent
911	    # smart_grad term (1−gate)·alpha·mu, mu=rescale·phi, is well ABOVE the param
912	    # tolerance (1e-4). With the default rescale=0.1 the mu term is too small to move
913	    # params measurably, so a wrong gate (cos(grad,mu) vs cos(grad,momentum)) hides
914	    # under the tolerance even when the gates diverge by ~0.8 — the param check would
915	    # falsely PASS the OLD kernel. A big rescale makes the gate genuinely load-bearing.
916	    import torch as _t
917	    opt_obj = spec["factory"](g, m.parameters(), c)
918	    with _t.no_grad():
919	        opt_obj.meta_net.rescale.fill_(2.0)
920	    opt_obj._weights_dirty = True
921	    named0 = [(n, p) for n, p in m.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]
922	    total = sum(p.numel() for _, p in named0)
923	
924	    def _flat_params():
925	        out = torch.empty(total, device=dev); o = 0
926	        for _, p in named0:
927	            k = p.numel(); out[o:o + k].copy_(p.data.reshape(-1)); o += k
928	        return out
929	
930	    # ── WARM-UP: run `warmup_steps` real steps so exp_avg (momentum) becomes nonzero.
931	    cache = {}
932	    for s in range(1, warmup_steps + 1):
933	        fused_train_step(canon, opt, m, opt_obj, tx, ty, state_cache=cache,
934	                         step=s, return_grad=False, gemm_impl="wgmma")
935	
936	    # Start-of-step state going INTO the gated step (= the kernel's st.exp_avg/
937	    # exp_avg_sq/params at gate time): the cache m/v slices + the live (warmed) params.
938	    kstate = cache[canon]["state"]
939	    m_start = kstate[0:total].clone()
940	    v_start = kstate[total:2 * total].clone()
941	    p_start = _flat_params()
942	    mom_norm = float(m_start.norm())
943	    t_step = warmup_steps + 1
944	
945	    # ── GATED step (step = warmup_steps+1) on the SAME cache (so it reads the warmed
946	    # momentum), capturing the TC-reduced grad + post-step params (the kernel's gate
947	    # now uses cos(grad, m_start)).
948	    loss, grad = fused_train_step(canon, opt, m, opt_obj, tx, ty, state_cache=cache,
949	                                  step=t_step, return_grad=True, gemm_impl="wgmma")
950	    p_after = _flat_params()
951	
952	    # ── (A)/(B) THE DIRECT GATE SURFACE — recover the kernel's ACTUAL per-tensor gate
953	    # and compare it to BOTH formulations. This is the load-bearing instrument: the
954	    # post-Adam params and even the m-state are heavily damped (β1·m0 + 0.1·smart_grad,
955	    # then v-normalized), so a wrong gate is washed out below the 1e-4 param/state
956	    # tolerance even when the two gate FORMULATIONS differ by ~0.8. The gate itself is
957	    # NOT damped, so recovering it exposes the bug cleanly.
958	    #
959	    # The kernel wrote k_m = β1·m0 + (1−β1)·smart_grad with smart_grad = g + (1−gate)·
960	    # alpha·mu and a per-TENSOR scalar gate. So smart_grad_kernel = (k_m − β1·m0)/(1−β1),
961	    # and (1−gate)·alpha = <smart_grad_kernel − g, mu> / <mu, mu> (least-squares over the
962	    # tensor since gate is one scalar). gate_kernel = 1 − that/alpha. Compare to:
963	    #   gate_momentum = sigmoid(gate_temp·cos(grad, m0))   — CANONICAL (FIXED kernel)
964	    #   gate_mu       = sigmoid(gate_temp·cos(grad, k_mu)) — BUGGY     (OLD kernel)
965	    scalars = _opt_scalars_from(opt_obj, t_step)
966	    gate_temp = float(scalars.get("gate_temp", 5.0))
967	    alpha = float(scalars["alpha"]); beta1 = float(scalars["beta1"])
968	    k_mu = kstate[2 * total:3 * total]
969	    k_m = kstate[0:total]
970	    off = 0; gate_div = 0.0
971	    err_vs_momentum = 0.0   # |gate_kernel − gate_momentum|  → ~0 for FIXED, large for OLD
972	    err_vs_mu = 0.0         # |gate_kernel − gate_mu|        → ~0 for OLD,   large for FIXED
973	    for n_, p in named0:
974	        k = p.numel()
975	        gt = grad[off:off + k].double()
976	        mut = k_mu[off:off + k].double()
977	        m0 = m_start[off:off + k].double()
978	        km = k_m[off:off + k].double()
979	        m0b = m_start[off:off + k].double()
980	        def _gate(b):
981	            num = (gt * b).sum()
982	            den = torch.sqrt((gt * gt).sum() * (b * b).sum() + 1e-12)
983	            cos = float(num / den) if den > 0 else 0.0
984	            return 1.0 / (1.0 + math.exp(-gate_temp * cos))

986	        gate_div = max(gate_div, abs(g_mom - g_mu))
987	        # Recover the kernel's gate from the m-state (per-tensor least-squares).
988	        sg_k = (km - beta1 * m0b) / (1.0 - beta1)
989	        denom = float((mut * mut).sum())
990	        if denom > 1e-20 and alpha > 1e-12:

1	"""tests/hw/sg2_kernel_mirror.py — single-threaded STRUCTURAL mirror of the
2	SuperGrok2 meta-net MEGAKERNEL (csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh).
3	
4	WHY (the gate the math-oracle cannot provide): the per-op SG2 path
5	(grokking_optimizers/kernels/sm_90/supergrok2_sm90.cuh :: csa_hca_step_one) is
6	parity-validated and is the MATH oracle. It does NOT exercise the MEGAKERNEL's
7	*structure* — the per-CTA workspace carving + REUSE (q staged with g/s then
8	copied into win_k/win_v; concat reused csa→hca), the sorted/original index
9	juggling (perm/unsort), the hand-written sequential GRU/PEER reductions, the
10	low-rank-only indexer, the insertion-sort top-k. That structure is exactly where
11	a hand-written, un-runnable kernel hides a dead-buffer read / an index bug / a
12	missing unsort (e.g. attention reading a `concat` slot HCA already overwrote, or
13	PEER reading `new_gru` from the wrong row order).
14	
15	This module re-implements the KERNEL ALGORITHM in plain Python — SAME buffers
16	(as a dict of fp64 arrays), SAME aliasing decisions (q→g/s→win_k/win_v, concat
17	csa→hca reuse), SAME loop nests / index math (sorted-row owner-computes,
18	perm/unsort gather) — and asserts it against an INDEPENDENT fp64 ORACLE that
19	reimplements csa_hca_step_one's math cleanly (different buffers, vectorized).
20	Agreement to ~1e-12 (fp64) catches the STRUCTURAL bug class. Single-threaded, so
21	it does NOT catch __syncthreads races (those are verified by reading each sync
22	against the buffer it guards — see the .cuh stage comments); it DOES catch
23	everything else.
24	
25	IMPORTANT — the ORACLE is csa_hca_step_one, NOT the eager CSAHCAMetaNet.forward.
26	The eager net's lightning indexer is FULL-RANK ( (x@idx_DQ)@idx_UQ ), while the
27	kernel path is LOW-RANK only ( qI=x@idx_DQ, kI=pooled(x)@idx_K, rank-dim dot ) —
28	they select different top-k by construction. The parity-validated path is the
29	CUDA kernel path, so that is the 1e-12 target here. The transcendentals match the
30	kernel: ptx_expf (≈ accurate in fp64) is just exp in the mirror; the kernel uses
31	accurate expf in GRU/PEER and ptx_expf in attention/compress, both of which are
32	ordinary exp at fp64 precision, so the mirror/oracle agree exactly in fp64.

106	def _csa_pooled(x_seq, compress_w, j, dd, N, d, m, win):
107	    """sg2_csa_compress_kv: online-softmax weighted pool over the window."""
108	    base = j * m
109	    run_max = -math.inf
110	    for wq in range(win):
111	        if base + wq >= N:
112	            break
113	        run_max = max(run_max, compress_w[wq])
114	    if not math.isfinite(run_max):
115	        return 0.0
116	    denom = 0.0

118	    for wq in range(win):
119	        t = base + wq
120	        if t >= N:
121	            break
122	        e = math.exp(compress_w[wq] - run_max)
123	        denom += e
124	        acc += e * x_seq[t, dd]

142	def _attn_accum(q, k, v, run_max, run_denom, acc, scale, hd):
143	    """sg2_attention_score_and_accumulate (online softmax)."""
144	    dot = 0.0
145	    for e in range(hd):
146	        dot += q[e] * k[e]
147	    s = dot * scale
148	    m_old = run_max
149	    m_new = max(m_old, s)
150	    corr = math.exp(m_old - m_new)
151	    p = math.exp(s - m_new)
152	    run_denom = run_denom * corr + p
153	    for e in range(hd):
154	        acc[e] = acc[e] * corr + p * v[e]

158	def _online_attn_reference(qh, kh, vh, sel_idx, winkh, winvh, scale, D):
159	    """REFERENCE (slow, per-scalar) online-softmax attention — the EXACT body
160	    of the original ``online_attn`` closure inside ``oracle_step``, lifted to a
161	    module-level function so the self-test can compare the vectorized path
162	    against it. Combines, per (query t, head h), an online softmax over the
163	    UNION of (a) the selected key rows ``sel_idx[t]`` (or ALL key rows when
164	    ``sel_idx is None``, the HCA case), filtered to ``0<=s<M``, and (b) the
165	    causal window rows ``range(max(t-csa_window+1,0), t+1)`` scored against
166	    ``winkh``/``winvh``. ``qh:[N,H,hd]``, ``kh``/``vh:[M,H,hd]``,
167	    ``winkh``/``winvh:[N,H,hd]``."""

169	    ctx = np.zeros((N, H, hd), _F64)
170	    for t in range(N):
171	        for h in range(H):
172	            rm = -math.inf
173	            rd = 0.0
174	            acc = np.zeros(hd, _F64)
175	            keys = sel_idx[t] if sel_idx is not None else range(kh.shape[0])
176	            for s in keys:
177	                if s < 0 or s >= kh.shape[0]:
178	                    continue
179	                sc = float(qh[t, h] @ kh[s, h]) * scale
180	                nm = max(rm, sc)
181	                corr = math.exp(rm - nm)
182	                p = math.exp(sc - nm)
183	                rd = rd * corr + p
184	                acc = acc * corr + p * vh[s, h]
185	                rm = nm
186	            # window over raw-token projections (win_k/win_v).
187	            w0 = max(t - D.csa_window + 1, 0)
188	            for s in range(w0, t + 1):
189	                sc = float(qh[t, h] @ winkh[s, h]) * scale
190	                nm = max(rm, sc)
191	                corr = math.exp(rm - nm)
192	                p = math.exp(sc - nm)
193	                rd = rd * corr + p
194	                acc = acc * corr + p * winvh[s, h]
195	                rm = nm
196	            ctx[t, h] = acc / rd if rd > 0 else acc
197	    return ctx.reshape(N, D.d_model)

200	def _online_attn_vectorized(qh, kh, vh, sel_idx_arr, winkh, winvh, scale, D):
201	    """VECTORIZED equivalent of ``_online_attn_reference``. Mathematically
202	    identical to fp64 rounding (softmax is permutation-invariant, so a single
203	    numerically-stable softmax over the combined {selected-key, window} logits
204	    reproduces the streaming online softmax exactly).
205	
206	    ``sel_idx_arr`` is either ``None`` (HCA: every key row is a key for every
207	    query) or an int array ``[N, topk]`` of selected compressed-key rows (the
208	    CSA case; entries ``<0`` or ``>=M`` are masked out, matching the reference's
209	    ``if s<0 or s>=M: continue``). The exact key SET and the exact value vector
210	    each key contributes are preserved: selected keys contribute ``vh[s]`` and
211	    window keys contribute ``winvh[s]``, kept as DISTINCT entries (no dedup)."""
212	    N, H, hd = qh.shape
213	    M = kh.shape[0]
214	    neg_inf = -np.inf
215	
216	    # ---- selected-key (or all-key) block ----
217	    if sel_idx_arr is None:
218	        # HCA: every one of the M key rows is a key for every query.
219	        # logits_sel[t, j, h] = (qh[t,h] . kh[j,h]) * scale
220	        logits_sel = np.einsum("thd,jhd->tjh", qh, kh, optimize=True) * scale  # [N,M,H]
221	        val_sel = vh                                                            # [M,H,hd]
222	        sel_gather = None
223	        sel_valid = None  # all valid
224	    else:
225	        sel = sel_idx_arr                                   # [N, topk] int
226	        sel_valid = (sel >= 0) & (sel < M)                  # [N, topk]
227	        sel_clamped = np.where(sel_valid, sel, 0)           # safe gather index
228	        # gather keys/values for each (t, slot): [N, topk, H, hd]
229	        kh_sel = kh[sel_clamped]
230	        val_sel = vh[sel_clamped]                           # [N, topk, H, hd]
231	        # logits[t, slot, h] = sum_hd qh[t,h,:] * kh_sel[t,slot,h,:]
232	        logits_sel = np.einsum("thd,tshd->tsh", qh, kh_sel, optimize=True) * scale  # [N,topk,H]
233	        logits_sel = np.where(sel_valid[:, :, None], logits_sel, neg_inf)
234	        sel_gather = val_sel
235	
236	    # ---- causal window block ----
237	    W = D.csa_window
238	    t_idx = np.arange(N)
239	    # window rows for query t are [t-W+1, ..., t]; columns ordered ascending.
240	    win_cols = t_idx[:, None] - np.arange(W - 1, -1, -1)[None, :]   # [N, W]
241	    win_valid = win_cols >= 0                                       # [N, W]
242	    win_clamped = np.where(win_valid, win_cols, 0)
243	    winkh_w = winkh[win_clamped]                                    # [N, W, H, hd]
244	    winvh_w = winvh[win_clamped]
245	    logits_win = np.einsum("thd,twhd->twh", qh, winkh_w, optimize=True) * scale  # [N,W,H]
246	    logits_win = np.where(win_valid[:, :, None], logits_win, neg_inf)
247	
248	    # ---- combined numerically-stable softmax over the union ----
249	    if sel_idx_arr is None:
250	        m_sel = logits_sel.max(axis=1)                              # [N,H]
251	    else:
252	        m_sel = logits_sel.max(axis=1)                              # [N,H] (>=neg_inf)
253	    m_win = logits_win.max(axis=1)                                  # [N,H]
254	    m = np.maximum(m_sel, m_win)                                    # [N,H] global max
255	    m_safe = np.where(np.isfinite(m), m, 0.0)                       # avoid -inf - -inf
256	
257	    p_sel = np.exp(logits_sel - m_safe[:, None, :])                # [N,S,H]; masked->0
258	    p_win = np.exp(logits_win - m_safe[:, None, :])                # [N,W,H]; masked->0
259	
260	    rd = p_sel.sum(axis=1) + p_win.sum(axis=1)                      # [N,H]
261	
262	    # numerator: sum_s p_sel * val_sel  +  sum_w p_win * winvh_w
263	    if sel_idx_arr is None:
264	        num = np.einsum("tjh,jhd->thd", p_sel, val_sel, optimize=True)        # [N,H,hd]
265	    else:
266	        num = np.einsum("tsh,tshd->thd", p_sel, sel_gather, optimize=True)    # [N,H,hd]
267	    num = num + np.einsum("twh,twhd->thd", p_win, winvh_w, optimize=True)     # [N,H,hd]
268	
269	    rd_safe = np.where(rd > 0.0, rd, 1.0)
270	    ctx = np.where(rd[:, :, None] > 0.0, num / rd_safe[:, :, None], num)      # [N,H,hd]
271	    return ctx.reshape(N, D.d_model)
272

275	#  THE STRUCTURAL MIRROR — follows opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh stage-for-stage,
276	#  including the workspace REUSE/ALIASING. `ws` is a dict of fp64 arrays mirroring

280	def mirror_step(w, grad, sharp, perm, unsort, gru_state, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq,

284	    (sorted), csa_ctx, hca_ctx, new_gru (sorted) for assertions."""
285	    N = grad.shape[0]
286	    d = D.d_model
287	    hd = D.head_dim
288	    rk = D.indexer_rank
289	    gh = D.gru_hidden
290	    Nc = (N + D.csa_compress - 1) // D.csa_compress
291	    Nh = (N + D.hca_compress - 1) // D.hca_compress
292	    topk = min(D.csa_topk, Nc)

299	        csa_ctx=np.zeros((N, d), _F64),
300	        hca_ctx=np.zeros((N, d), _F64),
301	        q=np.zeros((N, d), _F64),
302	        c_k=np.zeros((Nc, d), _F64),
303	        c_v=np.zeros((Nc, d), _F64),
304	        win_k=np.zeros((N, d), _F64),   # NOTE: also reused as g_sorted/[N] later
305	        win_v=np.zeros((N, d), _F64),   # NOTE: also reused as s_sorted/[N] later

314	    # S0: input projection + gather sorted features (fused: sorted-row owner).
315	    for r in range(N):
316	        src = perm[r]
317	        g = grad[src]
318	        s = sharp[src]
319	        if not np.isfinite(g):
320	            g = 0.0
321	        if not np.isfinite(s):

443	            ak = av = 0.0
444	            for k in range(d):

447	            ws["win_k"][t, oc] = ak
448	            ws["win_v"][t, oc] = av
449	    for t in range(N):

452	            acc = [0.0] * hd

607	        ws["expert_out"][r] = head_sum * scalars["rescale"]

611	    bc2 = max(scalars["bc2"], 1e-30)
612	    for i in range(N):
613	        eo = ws["expert_out"][unsort[i]]
614	        g = grad[i]
615	        p = param[i]
616	        mu_new = scalars["gru_decay"] * mu[i] + (1.0 - scalars["gru_decay"]) * eo
617	        mu[i] = mu_new
618	        slow_new = scalars["alpha"] * slow[i] + (1.0 - scalars["alpha"]) * g
619	        slow[i] = slow_new
620	        smart = g + scalars["alpha"] * mu_new + scalars["lamb_eff"] * slow_new
621	        m = scalars["beta1"] * exp_avg[i] + (1.0 - scalars["beta1"]) * smart
622	        v = scalars["beta2"] * exp_avg_sq[i] + (1.0 - scalars["beta2"]) * smart * smart
623	        exp_avg[i] = m
624	        exp_avg_sq[i] = v
625	        update = (m / bc1) / (math.sqrt(v / bc2) + scalars["eps"])
626	        param[i] = p - scalars["lr"] * (update + scalars["wd"] * p)
627	
628	    return dict(expert_out=ws["expert_out"].copy(),
629	                csa_ctx=ws["csa_ctx"].copy(),
630	                hca_ctx=ws["hca_ctx"].copy(),
631	                new_gru=ws["new_gru"].copy())
632	
633	
634	# ============================================================================
635	#  THE INDEPENDENT ORACLE — reimplements csa_hca_step_one's math CLEANLY
636	#  (vectorized numpy, fresh buffers, NO kernel aliasing). Same math, different
637	#  structure → asserting mirror == oracle isolates STRUCTURE bugs.
638	# ============================================================================
639	def _csa_topk_select(qI, kI, inv_sqrt_rk, topk):
640	    """Per-query top-`topk` compressed keys from the CSA low-rank indexer scores
641	    S = (qI @ kI.T) * inv_sqrt_rk, returned in DESCENDING score order ([N, k]).
642	
643	    This O(N·Nc) selection (Nc = kI.shape[0] ≈ N/csa_compress) is the single
644	    dominant cost of the oracle at real param-tensor sizes (N up to ~65K ⇒ an N×Nc
645	    ≈ 1e9-element score matrix); the naive full per-row stable argsort made the SG2
646	    gate cells effectively hang. The SELECTION is a discrete ranking (WHICH
647	    compressed keys) — NOT the meta-net math — and the production kernel itself
648	    computes this indexer in bf16/fp32 on the GPU, so doing the score matmul + top-k
649	    on the GPU (or in fp32 on the CPU) is faithful to the kernel. The fp64
650	    ground-truth that matters (attention weights, GRU/PEER/Adam) is untouched, and
651	    for tie-free scores the selected SET is identical across fp64/fp32/GPU; the
652	    downstream attention softmax over that set is permutation-invariant, so neither
653	    the dtype of the ranking nor the intra-k order changes csa_ctx.
654	
655	    Fast path: torch on CUDA (matmul + torch.topk, fp32) — milliseconds on an H100.
656	    Fallback: chunked numpy argpartition (fp32 scores, bounded peak memory) when
657	    CUDA/torch is unavailable (e.g. the standalone CPU `--selftest`)."""
658	    N = qI.shape[0]
659	    Nc = kI.shape[0]
660	    k = min(topk, Nc)
661	    # --- GPU fast path (the gate runs with torch+CUDA available) ---
662	    try:
663	        import torch
664	        if torch.cuda.is_available():
665	            with torch.no_grad():
666	                q = torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(qI, dtype=np.float32)).cuda()
667	                kk = torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(kI, dtype=np.float32)).cuda()
668	                sc = (q @ kk.T) * float(inv_sqrt_rk)              # [N, Nc] fp32 (GPU)
669	                idx = torch.topk(sc, k, dim=1, largest=True, sorted=True).indices
670	                out = idx.to("cpu").numpy().astype(np.intp)
671	                del q, kk, sc, idx
672	                return out
673	    except Exception:
674	        pass  # fall through to the pure-numpy path
675	    # --- numpy fallback: chunked top-k via argpartition (no full O(Nc·logNc) sort) ---
676	    qI32 = np.ascontiguousarray(qI, dtype=np.float32)
677	    kI32T = np.ascontiguousarray(kI.T, dtype=np.float32)
678	    inv32 = np.float32(inv_sqrt_rk)
679	    sel = np.empty((N, k), dtype=np.intp)
680	    _BLK = 16384
681	    for _s in range(0, N, _BLK):
682	        _e = min(_s + _BLK, N)
683	        blk = (qI32[_s:_e] @ kI32T) * inv32                      # [b, Nc] fp32
684	        if k >= Nc:
685	            sel[_s:_e] = np.argsort(-blk, axis=1, kind="stable")[:, :k]
686	        else:
687	            part = np.argpartition(blk, Nc - k, axis=1)[:, Nc - k:]  # unordered top-k
688	            ps = np.take_along_axis(blk, part, axis=1)
689	            order = np.argsort(-ps, axis=1, kind="stable")          # order the k (cheap)
690	            sel[_s:_e] = np.take_along_axis(part, order, axis=1)
691	    return sel
692	
693	
694	def oracle_step(w, grad, sharp, perm, unsort, gru_state, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq,
695	                mu, slow, param, scalars, D=Dims):
696	    N = grad.shape[0]
697	    d = D.d_model
698	    hd = D.head_dim
699	    rk = D.indexer_rank
700	    gh = D.gru_hidden
701	    Nc = (N + D.csa_compress - 1) // D.csa_compress
702	    Nh = (N + D.hca_compress - 1) // D.hca_compress
703	    topk = max(min(D.csa_topk, Nc), 1)
704	    scale = 1.0 / math.sqrt(hd)
705	    H = D.num_heads
706	
707	    g_all = grad.astype(_F64)
708	    s_all = sharp.astype(_F64)
709	    g_all = np.where(np.isfinite(g_all), g_all, 0.0)
710	    s_all = np.where(np.isfinite(s_all), s_all, 0.0)
711	
712	    # input proj on sorted rows.
713	    g_sorted = g_all[perm]
714	    s_sorted = s_all[perm]
715	    inp = np.stack([g_sorted, s_sorted], axis=-1)              # [N,2]
716	    x_sorted = inp @ w["input_proj_W"].T + w["input_proj_b"]   # [N,d]
717	
718	    def softmax_pool_csa():
719	        # weighted pooled x for each (j, channel) via online softmax over window.
720	        cw = w["csa_compress_w"]
721	        out = np.zeros((Nc, d), _F64)
722	        for j in range(Nc):
723	            base = j * D.csa_compress
724	            taps = [base + wq for wq in range(D.csa_window) if base + wq < N]
725	            if not taps:
726	                continue
727	            logits = np.array([cw[t - base] for t in taps], _F64)
728	            m = logits.max()
729	            e = np.exp(logits - m)
730	            wts = e / e.sum()
731	            out[j] = (wts[:, None] * x_sorted[taps]).sum(0)
732	        return out
733	
734	    def meanpool_hca():
735	        out = np.zeros((Nh, d), _F64)
736	        for j in range(Nh):
737	            base = j * D.hca_compress
738	            taps = [base + wq for wq in range(D.hca_compress) if base + wq < N]
739	            if taps:
740	                out[j] = x_sorted[taps].mean(0)
741	        return out
742	
743	    pooled_csa = softmax_pool_csa()       # [Nc, d]  (pooled raw features)
744	
745	    def heads(t):
746	        return t.reshape(t.shape[0], H, hd)
747	
748	    def online_attn(qh, kh, vh, sel_idx, window_only=False):
749	        # qh:[N,H,hd]; kh/vh:[M,H,hd]; sel_idx: per-query key rows (compressed),
750	        # an int array [N,topk] (CSA) or None (HCA: all M key rows). winkh/winvh
751	        # are read from the enclosing oracle_step scope (the window projections).
752	        # Dispatch to vectorized or reference body; both are fp64-identical.
753	        if _USE_VECTORIZED:
754	            return _online_attn_vectorized(qh, kh, vh, sel_idx, winkh, winvh,
755	                                           scale, D)
756	        # Reference path needs sel_idx as a per-row iterable; the vectorized
757	        # path passes an array, the reference accepts either (None or [N,topk]).
758	        return _online_attn_reference(qh, kh, vh, sel_idx, winkh, winvh,
759	                                      scale, D)
760	
761	    # CSA
762	    q_csa = heads(x_sorted @ w["csa_q_W"].T)
763	    c_k = (pooled_csa @ w["csa_k_W"].T)
764	    c_v = (pooled_csa @ w["csa_v_W"].T)
765	    c_kh = heads(c_k); c_vh = heads(c_v)
766	    winkh = heads(x_sorted @ w["csa_k_W"].T)
767	    winvh = heads(x_sorted @ w["csa_v_W"].T)
768	    qI = x_sorted @ w["csa_idx_DQ"]                       # [N, rk]
769	    kI = pooled_csa @ w["csa_idx_K"]                      # [Nc, rk]
770	    # CSA low-rank indexer top-k (the O(N·Nc) dominant cost — see _csa_topk_select).
771	    # Reproduces the same per-row top-`topk` of (qI@kI.T)/sqrt(rk) in descending
772	    # score; GPU-accelerated when available, chunked-numpy fallback otherwise.
773	    inv_sqrt_rk = 1.0 / math.sqrt(rk)
774	    sel_idx = _csa_topk_select(qI, kI, inv_sqrt_rk, topk)   # [N, topk] descending
775	    csa_ctx = online_attn(q_csa, c_kh, c_vh, sel_idx)
776	    csa_ctx = csa_ctx @ w["csa_out_W"].T
777	
778	    # HCA
779	    pooled_hca = meanpool_hca()
780	    q_hca = heads(x_sorted @ w["hca_q_W"].T)
781	    hk = heads(pooled_hca @ w["hca_k_W"].T)
782	    hv = heads(pooled_hca @ w["hca_v_W"].T)
783	    winkh = heads(x_sorted @ w["hca_k_W"].T)
784	    winvh = heads(x_sorted @ w["hca_v_W"].T)
785	    hca_ctx = online_attn(q_hca, hk, hv, None)
786	    hca_ctx = hca_ctx @ w["hca_out_W"].T
787	
788	    # matrix-GRU (sorted)
789	    h_old = gru_state[perm].astype(_F64)                 # [N, gh]
790	    gru_input = np.concatenate(
791	        [g_sorted[:, None], s_sorted[:, None], csa_ctx, hca_ctx], axis=-1)
792	    xh = np.concatenate([gru_input, h_old], axis=-1)
793	    z = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-(xh @ w["gru_Wz"].T + w["gru_bz"])))
794	    r = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-(xh @ w["gru_Wr"].T + w["gru_br"])))
795	    xrh = np.concatenate([gru_input, r * h_old], axis=-1)
796	    h_tilde = np.tanh(xrh @ w["gru_Wh"].T + w["gru_bh"])
797	    new_gru = (1.0 - z) * h_old + z * h_tilde            # [N, gh] sorted
798	    # persist in original order
799	    new_gru_orig = np.zeros_like(new_gru)
800	    new_gru_orig[perm] = new_gru
801	    gru_state[...] = new_gru_orig
802	
803	    # PEER (sorted)
804	    peer_input = np.concatenate(
805	        [new_gru, csa_ctx, hca_ctx, g_sorted[:, None], s_sorted[:, None]], axis=-1)
806	    half = d // 2
807	    pkd = D.pk_dim
808	    K = D.peer_topk
809	    T = 10.0
810	    total = np.zeros(N, _F64)
811	    for h in range(D.num_peer_heads):
812	        query = peer_input @ w["peer_query_Ws"][h].T     # [N, d]
813	        qa = query[:, :half]
814	        qb = query[:, half:]
815	        sa = qa @ w["prod_keys_A"][h].T                  # [N, pk_dim]
816	        sb = qb @ w["prod_keys_B"][h].T
817	        ka = min(K, pkd)
818	        kb = ka
819	        ta_i = np.argsort(-sa, axis=1, kind="stable")[:, :ka]
820	        tb_i = np.argsort(-sb, axis=1, kind="stable")[:, :kb]
821	        ta_v = np.take_along_axis(sa, ta_i, axis=1)
822	        tb_v = np.take_along_axis(sb, tb_i, axis=1)
823	        soft_a = np.exp((ta_v - ta_v.max(1, keepdims=True)) * T)
824	        soft_a /= soft_a.sum(1, keepdims=True)
825	        soft_b = np.exp((tb_v - tb_v.max(1, keepdims=True)) * T)
826	        soft_b /= soft_b.sum(1, keepdims=True)
827	        if _USE_VECTORIZED:
828	            # Vectorize over t and the ka*kb (ia,ib) expert pairs. The (ia,ib)
829	            # accumulation is an order-independent sum, so a batched reduction
830	            # reproduces head_out[t] exactly (fp64 rounding).
831	            # eidx[t,ia,ib] = clip(ta_i[t,ia]*pkd + tb_i[t,ib], 0, num_experts-1)
832	            eidx = ta_i[:, :, None] * pkd + tb_i[:, None, :]          # [N,ka,kb]
833	            eidx = np.clip(eidx, 0, D.num_experts - 1)
834	            rw = soft_a[:, :, None] * soft_b[:, None, :]             # [N,ka,kb]
835	            # expert MLP on the scalar g_sorted[t]:
836	            #   z = relu(expert_W1[e]*g + expert_b1[e]) ; expert_W1/b1: [.,eh]
837	            #   mlp = expert_W2[e] @ z + expert_b2[e]   ; expert_W2: [.,eh]
838	            W1 = w["expert_W1"][eidx]                                # [N,ka,kb,eh]
839	            b1 = w["expert_b1"][eidx]                                # [N,ka,kb,eh]
840	            W2 = w["expert_W2"][eidx]                                # [N,ka,kb,eh]
841	            b2 = w["expert_b2"][eidx]                                # [N,ka,kb]
842	            gcol = g_sorted[:, None, None, None]                     # [N,1,1,1]
843	            zrelu = np.maximum(W1 * gcol + b1, 0.0)                  # [N,ka,kb,eh]
844	            mlp = np.einsum("abce,abce->abc", W2, zrelu, optimize=True) + b2  # [N,ka,kb]
845	            head_out = (rw * mlp).sum(axis=(1, 2))                   # [N]
846	        else:
847	            head_out = np.zeros(N, _F64)
848	            for t in range(N):
849	                for ia in range(ka):
850	                    for ib in range(kb):
851	                        eidx = int(ta_i[t, ia]) * pkd + int(tb_i[t, ib])
852	                        eidx = max(0, min(eidx, D.num_experts - 1))
853	                        rw = soft_a[t, ia] * soft_b[t, ib]
854	                        zrelu = np.maximum(
855	                            w["expert_W1"][eidx] * g_sorted[t] + w["expert_b1"][eidx], 0.0)
856	                        mlp = float(w["expert_W2"][eidx] @ zrelu) + w["expert_b2"][eidx]
857	                        head_out[t] += rw * mlp
858	        total += head_out
859	    total /= D.num_peer_heads
860	    expert_out_sorted = total * scalars["rescale"]
861	
862	    # apply (unsort), sg2_apply_step
863	    bc1 = max(scalars["bc1"], 1e-30)
864	    bc2 = max(scalars["bc2"], 1e-30)
865	    eo = expert_out_sorted[unsort]                       # back to original order
866	    g = g_all
867	    p = param.astype(_F64)
868	    mu_new = scalars["gru_decay"] * mu + (1.0 - scalars["gru_decay"]) * eo
869	    mu[...] = mu_new
870	    slow_new = scalars["alpha"] * slow + (1.0 - scalars["alpha"]) * g
871	    slow[...] = slow_new
872	    smart = g + scalars["alpha"] * mu_new + scalars["lamb_eff"] * slow_new
873	    m = scalars["beta1"] * exp_avg + (1.0 - scalars["beta1"]) * smart
874	    v = scalars["beta2"] * exp_avg_sq + (1.0 - scalars["beta2"]) * smart * smart
875	    exp_avg[...] = m
876	    exp_avg_sq[...] = v
877	    update = (m / bc1) / (np.sqrt(v / bc2) + scalars["eps"])
878	    param[...] = p - scalars["lr"] * (update + scalars["wd"] * p)
879	
880	    return dict(expert_out=expert_out_sorted, csa_ctx=csa_ctx, hca_ctx=hca_ctx,
881	                new_gru=new_gru)
882	
883	
884	def make_scalars():
885	    return dict(rescale=0.1, alpha=0.98, gru_decay=0.9, lamb_eff=2.0,
886	                beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, lr=1e-3, wd=0.01, eps=1e-8,
887	                bc1=1.0 - 0.9 ** 5, bc2=1.0 - 0.999 ** 5)
888	
889	
890	def make_sorted_perm(grad):
891	    """Reproduce csa_hca_step_one's sort: |grad| ASCENDING, stable.
892	       perm[r] = original row of the r-th sorted row;
893	       unsort[i] = sorted position of original row i."""
894	    perm = np.argsort(np.abs(grad), kind="stable").astype(np.int64)
895	    unsort = np.argsort(perm, kind="stable").astype(np.int64)
896	    return perm, unsort
897	
898	
899	# ============================================================================
900	#  SELF-TEST — vectorized oracle_step vs the retained reference (slow) path.
901	#  Asserts every output (in-place-mutated state + returned dict) agrees to
902	#  < 1e-9 (max-abs and max-rel) for a range of N, and that the vectorized
903	#  N=65536 path runs in < 1.0s. Pure numpy, CPU-only, no GPU/torch.
904	# ============================================================================
905	def _selftest(Ns=(16, 256, 1024, 16384, 65536), D=Dims, tol=1e-9, verbose=True):
906	    import copy as _copy
907	    import time as _time
908	
909	    global _USE_VECTORIZED
910	    gh = D.gru_hidden
911	    w = make_weights(seed=0, D=D)        # shared fp64 weights (Dims-consistent)
912	    scalars = make_scalars()
913	
914	    def _build_inputs(N, rng):
915	        # random grad/sharp + zero-init state (as the gate drives it), all fp64.
916	        grad = rng.standard_normal(N).astype(_F64)
917	        sharp = (rng.standard_normal(N) * 0.5).astype(_F64)
918	        perm, unsort = make_sorted_perm(grad)
919	        gru_state = rng.standard_normal((N, gh)).astype(_F64) * 0.1
920	        exp_avg = rng.standard_normal(N).astype(_F64) * 0.1
921	        exp_avg_sq = (np.abs(rng.standard_normal(N)) * 0.1).astype(_F64)
922	        mu = rng.standard_normal(N).astype(_F64) * 0.1
923	        slow = rng.standard_normal(N).astype(_F64) * 0.1
924	        param = rng.standard_normal(N).astype(_F64)
925	        return dict(grad=grad, sharp=sharp, perm=perm, unsort=unsort,
926	                    gru_state=gru_state, exp_avg=exp_avg, exp_avg_sq=exp_avg_sq,
927	                    mu=mu, slow=slow, param=param)
928	
929	    def _run(inp):
930	        # oracle_step mutates gru_state/exp_avg/exp_avg_sq/mu/slow/param in place.
931	        ret = oracle_step(w, inp["grad"], inp["sharp"], inp["perm"], inp["unsort"],
932	                          inp["gru_state"], inp["exp_avg"], inp["exp_avg_sq"],
933	                          inp["mu"], inp["slow"], inp["param"], scalars, D=D)
934	        out = dict(
935	            param=inp["param"], m=inp["exp_avg"], v=inp["exp_avg_sq"],
936	            mu=inp["mu"], slow=inp["slow"], gru_state=inp["gru_state"],
937	            expert_out=ret["expert_out"], csa_ctx=ret["csa_ctx"],
938	            hca_ctx=ret["hca_ctx"], new_gru=ret["new_gru"],
939	        )
940	        return out
941	
942	    def _err(a, b):
943	        a = np.asarray(a, _F64); b = np.asarray(b, _F64)
944	        diff = np.abs(a - b)
945	        max_abs = float(diff.max()) if diff.size else 0.0
946	        denom = np.maximum(np.abs(a), np.abs(b))
947	        rel = np.where(denom > 0, diff / denom, 0.0)
948	        max_rel = float(rel.max()) if rel.size else 0.0
949	        return max_abs, max_rel
950	
951	    all_ok = True
952	    for N in Ns:
953	        rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
954	        inp = _build_inputs(N, rng)
955	
956	        # reference (slow) path on a deep copy.
957	        _USE_VECTORIZED = False
958	        ref_out = _run(_copy.deepcopy(inp))
959	
960	        # vectorized path on a fresh deep copy + timing.
961	        _USE_VECTORIZED = True
962	        vinp = _copy.deepcopy(inp)
963	        t0 = _time.perf_counter()
964	        vec_out = _run(vinp)
965	        dt = _time.perf_counter() - t0
966	
967	        worst_abs = 0.0
968	        worst_rel = 0.0
969	        worst_key = ""
970	        for k in ref_out:
971	            ma, mr = _err(vec_out[k], ref_out[k])
972	            if ma > worst_abs:
973	                worst_abs, worst_key = ma, k
974	            worst_rel = max(worst_rel, mr)
975	        ok = (worst_abs < tol) and (worst_rel < tol)
976	        all_ok = all_ok and ok
977	        if N == 65536:
978	            ok = ok and (dt < 1.0)
979	            all_ok = all_ok and (dt < 1.0)
980	        if verbose:
981	            print(f"  N={N:6d}  max|Δ|={worst_abs:.3e} ({worst_key:10s})  "
982	                  f"max relΔ={worst_rel:.3e}  vec_time={dt:7.4f}s  "
983	                  f"{'OK' if ok else 'FAIL'}"
984	                  + ("  (<1.0s req)" if N == 65536 else ""))
985	
986	    _USE_VECTORIZED = True   # restore default fast path
987	    if verbose:
988	        print(f"\n  RESULT: {'ALL PASS' if all_ok else 'FAIL'} "
989	              f"(tol {tol:.0e}, N=65536 must be < 1.0s)")
990	    return all_ok
991	
992	
993	if __name__ == "__main__":
994	    import argparse
995	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="sg2_kernel_mirror self-test")
996	    ap.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true",
997	                    help="run vectorized-vs-reference oracle_step self-test")
998	    args = ap.parse_args()
999	    if args.selftest:
1000	        ok = _selftest()
1001	        raise SystemExit(0 if ok else 1)

39	#  Reference implementations (fp64 accumulate). One step, no in-place magic —

44	def _f64(t):
45	    return t.detach().to(torch.float64)
46

48	def _adam_tail(p, m_prev, v_prev, g_eff, lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2):
49	    """The shared bias-corrected Adam + decoupled-WD tail.
50	
51	    Bit-faithful (modulo fp32-vs-fp64 accumulation) to the tail repeated across
52	    adamw.h / grokadamw.h / grokfast.h / neuralgrok.h / looksam.h / prodigy.h /
53	    supergrok{11,15,2}.h:
54	
55	        m = beta1*m_prev + (1-beta1)*g_eff
56	        v = beta2*v_prev + (1-beta2)*g_eff*g_eff
57	        update = (m / bc1) / (sqrt(v / bc2) + eps)
58	        p_new  = p - lr * (update + wd * p)
59	    """
60	    m = beta1 * m_prev + (1.0 - beta1) * g_eff
61	    v = beta2 * v_prev + (1.0 - beta2) * g_eff * g_eff
62	    update = (m / bc1) / (torch.sqrt(v / bc2) + eps)
63	    p_new = p - lr * (update + wd * p)
64	    return p_new, m, v
65

67	# ── adamw.h ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
68	def ref_adamw_step(p, g, m, v, *, lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, t):
69	    p, g, m, v = map(_f64, (p, g, m, v))
70	    bc1 = 1.0 - beta1 ** t
71	    bc2 = 1.0 - beta2 ** t
72	    return _adam_tail(p, m, v, g, lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2)
73

75	# ── lion.h ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
76	def ref_lion_step(p, g, ea, *, lr, beta1, beta2, wd):
77	    """interp = beta1*ea + (1-beta1)*g; p -= lr*(sign(interp) + wd*p);
78	       ea = beta2*ea + (1-beta2)*g.  sign(0)=0 (copysignf guarded against 0)."""
79	    p, g, ea = map(_f64, (p, g, ea))
80	    interp = beta1 * ea + (1.0 - beta1) * g
81	    s = torch.where(interp != 0, torch.sign(interp), torch.zeros_like(interp))
82	    p_new = p - lr * (s + wd * p)
83	    ea_new = beta2 * ea + (1.0 - beta2) * g
84	    return p_new, ea_new

87	# ── grokadamw.h ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
88	def ref_grokadamw_step(p, g, m, v, ema, *, alpha, lamb, lr, beta1, beta2,
89	                       eps, wd, t):
90	    p, g, m, v, ema = map(_f64, (p, g, m, v, ema))
91	    ema_new = alpha * ema + (1.0 - alpha) * g
92	    g_amp = g + lamb * ema_new
93	    bc1 = 1.0 - beta1 ** t
94	    bc2 = 1.0 - beta2 ** t
95	    p_new, m_new, v_new = _adam_tail(p, m, v, g_amp, lr, beta1, beta2, eps,
96	                                     wd, bc1, bc2)
97	    return p_new, m_new, v_new, ema_new

109	def ref_neuralgrok_step(p, g, m, v, *, psi_scale, alpha, beta, lr, beta1,
110	                        beta2, eps, wd, t):
111	    """g_amp = (psi_scale*alpha + beta)*g; AdamW on g_amp.
112	       psi_scale is the psi-net (MLP) output, supplied per-element or scalar."""
113	    p, g, m, v = map(_f64, (p, g, m, v))
114	    if torch.is_tensor(psi_scale):
115	        psi_scale = _f64(psi_scale)
116	    g_amp = (psi_scale * alpha + beta) * g
117	    bc1 = 1.0 - beta1 ** t
118	    bc2 = 1.0 - beta2 ** t
119	    return _adam_tail(p, m, v, g_amp, lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2)

122	def ref_neuralgrok_psi_forward(abs_grad, W1, b1, W2, b2):
123	    """2-layer ReLU MLP forward (neuralgrok_psi_forward), fp64.
124	       W1,b1,W2: [H]; b2 scalar.  out = sum_j W2[j]*relu(W1[j]*|g| + b1[j]) + b2."""
125	    abs_grad, W1, b1, W2 = map(_f64, (abs_grad, W1, b1, W2))
126	    h = torch.relu(W1 * abs_grad.unsqueeze(-1) + b1)   # [..., H]
127	    return (h * W2).sum(-1) + b2

136	    bc2 = 1.0 - beta2 ** t
137	    return _adam_tail(p, m, v, g_adj, lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2)

150	# ── prodigy.h ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
151	def ref_prodigy_partials(p, p_init, g, *, d_prev):
152	    """r += g*(p_init - p)*d_prev^2 ; s += d_prev^2 * |g|  (global reductions).
153	
154	    Canonical form per csrc/algorithms/prodigy.h:48,52 (degree-2 d_prev makes
155	    d_hat scale-free; s uses the L1 norm |g|). An earlier revision of this ref
156	    used d_prev^1 and SIGNED g — stale vs the header; flagged by the opt-stages
157	    phase and fixed here so the header stays the single source of truth.
158	    """
159	    p, p_init, g = map(_f64, (p, p_init, g))
160	    r = (g * (p_init - p) * d_prev * d_prev).sum()
161	    s = (d_prev * d_prev * g.abs()).sum()
162	    return r, s

165	def ref_prodigy_update_d(d_prev, r_sum, s_sum):
166	    denom = abs(float(s_sum))
167	    if denom < 1e-12:
168	        return d_prev
169	    return max(d_prev, float(r_sum) / denom)

172	def ref_prodigy_apply_step(p, g, m, v, s_track, *, d, beta1, beta2, eps, wd,
173	                           t):
174	    """g_scaled = d*g; Adam moments on g_scaled; s_track += d*g;
175	       p -= d*(update + wd*p).  Note: the *step size* is d (not lr)."""
176	    p, g, m, v, s_track = map(_f64, (p, g, m, v, s_track))
177	    g_scaled = d * g
178	    bc1 = 1.0 - beta1 ** t
179	    bc2 = 1.0 - beta2 ** t
180	    mm = beta1 * m + (1.0 - beta1) * g_scaled
181	    vv = beta2 * v + (1.0 - beta2) * g_scaled * g_scaled
182	    s_track_new = s_track + d * g
183	    update = (mm / bc1) / (torch.sqrt(vv / bc2) + eps)
184	    p_new = p - d * (update + wd * p)
185	    return p_new, mm, vv, s_track_new

188	# ── supergrok11.h (sigmoid-of-cosine-gated meta-net) ─────────────────────────
189	def ref_sg11_step(p, g, m, v, mu, *, gate, alpha, lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, t):
190	    """smart_grad = g + (1 - gate)*alpha*mu; AdamW on smart_grad.
191	       gate is the pre-reduced gate = sigmoid(gate_temp * cos_sim(grad, momentum))
192	       (the canonical sg11_finalize_gate). Callers that compute the cosine feed
193	       its sigmoid in here (see sg11_gate_ref / parity_gate_h100._cosine_gate_ref /
194	       test_l3tc_tail_gate's per-tensor gate)."""
195	    p, g, m, v, mu = map(_f64, (p, g, m, v, mu))
196	    smart_grad = g + (1.0 - gate) * alpha * mu
197	    bc1 = 1.0 - beta1 ** t
198	    bc2 = 1.0 - beta2 ** t
199	    return _adam_tail(p, m, v, smart_grad, lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2)

202	def ref_sg_phi_forward(grad_val, sharp_val, W1, b1, W2, b2):
203	    """exact-GELU-hidden, linear-output meta-net (sg11/sg15 share the shape).
204	       W1: [H,2] flattened row-major; b1,W2: [H]; b2 scalar.
205	
206	       The canonical kernels use the EXACT erf GELU on the hidden pre-activation
207	       (csrc/algorithms/supergrok11.h:50-51, supergrok15.h:47-48:
208	       ``h = 0.5*h*(1 + erff(h * 0.70710678...))``), matching torch.nn.GELU() in
209	       the trainable meta-net — NOT a tanh hidden. This reference mirrors that
210	       exactly so the oracle does not silently diverge from the shipped phi-net.
211	    """
212	    grad_val, sharp_val, W1, b1, W2 = map(
213	        _f64, (grad_val, sharp_val, W1, b1, W2))
214	    W1 = W1.reshape(-1, 2)                       # [H, 2]
215	    pre = W1[:, 0] * grad_val + W1[:, 1] * sharp_val + b1
216	    # Exact GELU: 0.5*x*(1 + erf(x / sqrt(2))).
217	    gelu = 0.5 * pre * (1.0 + torch.erf(pre / math.sqrt(2.0)))
218	    return (gelu * W2).sum(-1) + b2
219

221	# ── supergrok15.h (sigmoid-accuracy-gated meta-net) ──────────────────────────
222	def ref_sg15_alpha_per_coord(mu_val, alpha_base, alpha_max):
223	    a = alpha_base * (1.0 + mu_val)
224	    return torch.clamp(a, 0.0, alpha_max)

227	def ref_sg15_step(p, g, m, v, mu, *, gate_global, alpha_base, alpha_max, lr,
228	                  beta1, beta2, eps, wd, t):
229	    """a = clamp(alpha_base*(1+mu), 0, alpha_max);
230	       smart_grad = g + gate_global*a*mu; AdamW on smart_grad."""
231	    p, g, m, v, mu = map(_f64, (p, g, m, v, mu))
232	    a = ref_sg15_alpha_per_coord(mu, alpha_base, alpha_max)
233	    smart_grad = g + gate_global * a * mu
234	    bc1 = 1.0 - beta1 ** t
235	    bc2 = 1.0 - beta2 ** t
236	    return _adam_tail(p, m, v, smart_grad, lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2)

239	# ── supergrok2.h (per-element GRU + expert EMA + slow-grad EMA, then Adam) ───
240	def ref_sg2_apply_step(p, g, m, v, mu_state, slow_state, *, expert_out, alpha,
241	                       gru_decay, lamb_eff, lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, t):
242	    """Mirrors csrc/algorithms/supergrok2.h::sg2_apply_step:
243	         mu_new   = gru_decay*mu_state + (1-gru_decay)*expert_out   (expert EMA)
244	         slow_new = alpha*slow_state   + (1-alpha)*g                (grokfast EMA)
245	         smart_grad = g + alpha*mu_new + lamb_eff*slow_new
246	       then AdamW on smart_grad. `alpha` is BOTH the mu/slow mixing coeff and the
247	       slow-EMA decay (matches the Python ref's alpha_i). lamb_eff is the
248	       restored grokfast amplification (lamb*ramp*gate); it was silently dropped
249	       (kernel (void)-ed lamb_eff) before this fix."""
250	    p, g, m, v, mu_state, slow_state = map(
251	        _f64, (p, g, m, v, mu_state, slow_state))
252	    if torch.is_tensor(expert_out):
253	        expert_out = _f64(expert_out)
254	    mu_new = gru_decay * mu_state + (1.0 - gru_decay) * expert_out
255	    slow_new = alpha * slow_state + (1.0 - alpha) * g
256	    smart_grad = g + alpha * mu_new + lamb_eff * slow_new
257	    bc1 = 1.0 - beta1 ** t
258	    bc2 = 1.0 - beta2 ** t
259	    p_new, m_new, v_new = _adam_tail(p, m, v, smart_grad, lr, beta1, beta2,
260	                                     eps, wd, bc1, bc2)
261	    return p_new, m_new, v_new, mu_new, slow_new

264	# ── muon.h (+ bindings.cpp::muon_fused_step orchestration) ───────────────────
265	# NS coefficients are the canonical (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) from
266	# csrc/bindings/bindings.cpp::muon_fused_step.
267	MUON_NS_A, MUON_NS_B, MUON_NS_C = 3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315
268	
269	
270	def ref_muon_step(p, g, buf, *, momentum, lr, wd, ns_steps):
271	    """2D parameter update.
272	        buf = momentum*buf + grad                 (no (1-momentum); matches header)
273	        X   = buf / (||buf||_F + 1e-7)
274	        repeat ns_steps:  A=X@Xᵀ; AX=A@X; AAX=A@AX; X = a*X + b*AX + c*AAX
275	        scale = 0.2 * sqrt(max(rows, cols))
276	        p     = p*(1 - lr*wd) + (-lr*scale)*X
277	    Returns (p_new, buf_new).
278	    """
279	    p, g, buf = map(_f64, (p, g, buf))
280	    buf_new = momentum * buf + g
281	    inv_norm = 1.0 / (torch.linalg.norm(buf_new) + 1e-7)
282	    X = buf_new * inv_norm
283	    for _ in range(ns_steps):
284	        A = X @ X.t()
285	        AX = A @ X
286	        AAX = A @ AX
287	        X = MUON_NS_A * X + MUON_NS_B * AX + MUON_NS_C * AAX
288	    rows, cols = p.shape[0], p.shape[1]
289	    scale = 0.2 * math.sqrt(max(rows, cols))
290	    neg_lr_scale = -lr * scale
291	    decay = 1.0 - lr * wd
292	    p_new = p * decay + neg_lr_scale * X
293	    return p_new, buf_new

337	def test_adamw_zero_grad_is_pure_weight_decay():
338	    p = _rand(8, seed=1)
339	    z = torch.zeros(8, dtype=torch.float64)
340	    # wd = 0  => exact no-op on the parameter
341	    p_new, m, v = ref_adamw_step(p, z, z.clone(), z.clone(),
342	                                 lr=1e-3, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999,
343	                                 eps=1e-8, wd=0.0, t=1)
344	    assert torch.allclose(p_new, p, atol=ATOL, rtol=RTOL)
345	    assert torch.allclose(m, z, atol=ATOL)
346	    assert torch.allclose(v, z, atol=ATOL)
347	    # wd > 0 => exactly the decoupled shrink p -= lr*wd*p (numerator is 0).
348	    lr, wd = 1e-3, 0.1
349	    p_wd, _, _ = ref_adamw_step(p, z, z.clone(), z.clone(),
350	                                lr=lr, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999,
351	                                eps=1e-8, wd=wd, t=1)
352	    assert torch.allclose(p_wd, p - lr * wd * p, atol=ATOL, rtol=RTOL)

391	# ── step-1 bias correction closed forms ──────────────────────────────────────
392	
393	def test_adamw_step1_bias_correction_closed_form():
394	    """At t=1 with m0=v0=0: m_hat = g, v_hat = g^2, so the Adam numerator
395	    collapses to sign(g) (modulo eps). p -= lr*(g/(|g|+eps) + wd*p)."""
396	    p = _rand(16, seed=5)
397	    g = _rand(16, seed=6)
398	    lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd = 1e-2, 0.9, 0.999, 1e-12, 0.0
399	    z = torch.zeros(16, dtype=torch.float64)
400	    p_new, m, v = ref_adamw_step(p, g, z.clone(), z.clone(),
401	                                 lr=lr, beta1=beta1, beta2=beta2,
402	                                 eps=eps, wd=wd, t=1)
403	    # bc1 = 1-beta1, bc2 = 1-beta2.  m_hat = (1-beta1)g / (1-beta1) = g.
404	    m_hat = m / (1.0 - beta1)
405	    v_hat = v / (1.0 - beta2)
406	    assert torch.allclose(m_hat, g, atol=ATOL, rtol=RTOL)
407	    assert torch.allclose(v_hat, g * g, atol=ATOL, rtol=RTOL)

463	    layers at indices i=0,1 must produce DIFFERENT first/second moments from the
464	    SAME grad — and gamma=0 must collapse to identical moments. Driven through
465	    the fp64 ref (no kernel) so it validates the β1 *formula*, not the build."""

470	                  wd=0.01, t=3)

476	                                        beta1=b1_i, **common)

709	def test_muon_ns_reduces_singular_value_spread():
710	    """The defining property of the Newton-Schulz orthogonalization: it drives
711	    a matrix toward the orthogonal manifold by *equalizing* its singular values
712	    (condition number -> 1). Assert the NS recurrence shrinks the spread of
713	    singular values (max/min ratio) on a tiny ill-conditioned matrix."""
714	    torch.manual_seed(3)
715	    M = torch.randn(4, 6, dtype=torch.float64)
716	    X = M / (torch.linalg.norm(M) + 1e-7)        # Frobenius-normalize (as Muon does)
717	    cond_before = (lambda s: (s.max() / s.min()))(torch.linalg.svdvals(X))
718	    for _ in range(5):
719	        A = X @ X.t()
720	        AX = A @ X
721	        AAX = A @ AX
722	        X = MUON_NS_A * X + MUON_NS_B * AX + MUON_NS_C * AAX
723	    cond_after = (lambda s: (s.max() / s.min()))(torch.linalg.svdvals(X))
724	    assert cond_after < cond_before, (float(cond_before), float(cond_after))
725	    # Substantially closer to orthonormal (was ~4.4, should drop well below 2).
726	    assert float(cond_after) < 2.0, float(cond_after)

256	#      R_t[h,c] = [[cos,-sin],[sin,cos]],  v_t = Bbar_t (.) x_t :
257	#
258	#      h_t = alpha_t * (R_t @ h_{t-1}) + beta_t * (R_t @ v_{t-1}) + gamma_t * v_t
259	#      y_t[b,h,p] = sum_{c,d} Cbar[t,c,d] * h_t[b,h,p,c,d]              (h_{-1}=0, v_{-1}=0)
260	#
261	#  with R(phi) @ (w0,w1) = (cos*w0 - sin*w1,  sin*w0 + cos*w1).
262	#
263	#  BACKWARD (reverse time t = L-1..0). Carry TWO adjoints:
264	#    gh[b,h,p,c,:] = dL/dh_t   (flows back through h_{t+1}=alpha R h_t + ...)
265	#    gv[b,h,p,c,:] = dL/dv_t   accumulated from step t+1's beta-term
266	#                              beta_{t+1} R_{t+1} v_t  (the WIDTH-2 coupling).
267	#  At step t:
268	#   1) y_t -> gh += Cbar_t * dy_t ;  dCbar[t] += sum_{b,h,p} h_t * dy_t .
269	#      Now gh = full dL/dh_t.
270	#   2) v_t's TOTAL grad: dv_t = gv + gamma_t * gh   (gv from t+1 beta; gamma at t).
271	#      v_t = Bbar_t (.) x_t  ->
272	#        dx[t,h,p] += sum_{c,d} dv_t[...,c,d] * Bbar[t,c,d]
273	#        dBbar[t,c,d] += sum_{b,h,p} dv_t[...,c,d] * x[t,h,p]
274	#   3) Rotated terms (need Rh = R_t @ h_{t-1}, Rv = R_t @ v_{t-1}):
275	#        dalpha[b,t,h] += sum_{p,c,d} Rh * gh
276	#        dbeta [b,t,h] += sum_{p,c,d} Rv * gh
277	#        dgamma[b,t,h] += sum_{p,c,d} v_t * gh
278	#      phi grad via R'(phi) [[-sin,-cos],[cos,-sin]] applied to h_{t-1} and v_{t-1}:
279	#        for a term coef*R@w with adjoint g:
280	#          dphi += coef*( g0*(-sin*w0 - cos*w1) + g1*(cos*w0 - sin*w1) )
281	#        dphi[b,t,h,c] += sum_p [ alpha*term(h_{t-1}) + beta*term(v_{t-1}) ]
282	#   4) Propagate to the previous step (R orthogonal -> adjoint uses R^T):
283	#        gv_next(=dL/dv_{t-1}) = beta_t * (R_t^T @ gh)     (carried to step t-1)
284	#        gh_next(=dL/dh_{t-1}) = alpha_t * (R_t^T @ gh)
285	#  After t=0 both carries multiply into h_{-1}=v_{-1}=0 and are discarded.
286	#
287	#  Then fold the coefficient Jacobians (all per head):
288	#    dt(post-softplus): ddt = dalpha*(A*alpha) + dbeta*((1-lam)*alpha*(1+dt*A))
289	#                            + dgamma*lam + sum_c dphi[...,c]*theta[t,c]
290	#    dlam            : dlam = dbeta*(-dt*alpha) + dgamma*dt
291	#    dA_real         : dA_real = dalpha*(dt*alpha) + dbeta*((1-lam)*dt^2*alpha)
292	#    dtheta (shared) : dtheta[t,c] = sum_h dphi[t,h,c]*dt[t,h]
293	#  R'(phi): d/dphi [cos,-sin;sin,cos] = [-sin,-cos;cos,-sin].  alpha=exp(dt*A):
294	#  dalpha/d(dt)=A*alpha, dalpha/dA=dt*alpha. beta=(1-lam)*dt*alpha. gamma=lam*dt.
295	# ===========================================================================
296	def scan_forward(x_h, dt, A_real, theta, lam, Bbar, Cbar, H, P, Nc):
297	    """x_h: [B,L,H,P] SSM input (no SiLU). dt,A_real,lam: [B,L,H] (per head).
298	    theta: [B,L,Nc] (head-shared). Bbar,Cbar: [B,L,Nc,2]. Returns (y, cache).
299	    y: [B,L,H,P]."""
300	    B, L, _, _ = x_h.shape
301	    dev, dt_t = x_h.device, x_h.dtype
302	    alpha = torch.exp(dt * A_real)              # [B,L,H]
303	    gamma = lam * dt                            # [B,L,H]
304	    beta = (1.0 - lam) * dt * alpha             # [B,L,H]
305	    phi = dt.unsqueeze(-1) * theta.unsqueeze(-2)  # [B,L,H,Nc]
306	    cos = torch.cos(phi)                        # [B,L,H,Nc]
307	    sin = torch.sin(phi)
308	
309	    h = torch.zeros(B, H, P, Nc, 2, dtype=dt_t, device=dev)
310	    v_prev = torch.zeros(B, H, P, Nc, 2, dtype=dt_t, device=dev)
311	    ys, h_hist, v_hist = [], [], []
312	    for t in range(L):
313	        x_t = x_h[:, t].view(B, H, P, 1, 1)            # [B,H,P,1,1]
314	        Bbar_t = Bbar[:, t].view(B, 1, 1, Nc, 2)       # [B,1,1,Nc,2]
315	        Cbar_t = Cbar[:, t].view(B, 1, 1, Nc, 2)
316	        v_t = Bbar_t * x_t                             # [B,H,P,Nc,2]
317	        cos_t = cos[:, t].view(B, H, 1, Nc)            # [B,H,1,Nc]
318	        sin_t = sin[:, t].view(B, H, 1, Nc)
319	        a_t = alpha[:, t].view(B, H, 1, 1, 1)
320	        b_t = beta[:, t].view(B, H, 1, 1, 1)
321	        g_t = gamma[:, t].view(B, H, 1, 1, 1)
322	        # rotate h_{t-1} and v_{t-1}
323	        hr, hi = h[..., 0], h[..., 1]
324	        Rh = torch.stack((cos_t * hr - sin_t * hi, sin_t * hr + cos_t * hi), -1)
325	        vr, vi = v_prev[..., 0], v_prev[..., 1]
326	        Rv = torch.stack((cos_t * vr - sin_t * vi, sin_t * vr + cos_t * vi), -1)
327	        h = a_t * Rh + b_t * Rv + g_t * v_t            # [B,H,P,Nc,2]
328	        h_hist.append(h)
329	        v_hist.append(v_t)
330	        y_t = (Cbar_t * h).sum(dim=(3, 4))             # [B,H,P]
331	        ys.append(y_t)
332	        v_prev = v_t
333	    y = torch.stack(ys, dim=1)                         # [B,L,H,P]
334	    cache = dict(x_h=x_h, dt=dt, A_real=A_real, theta=theta, lam=lam,
335	                 Bbar=Bbar, Cbar=Cbar, alpha=alpha, beta=beta, gamma=gamma,
336	                 cos=cos, sin=sin, h_hist=h_hist, v_hist=v_hist, H=H, P=P, Nc=Nc)
337	    return y, cache

340	def scan_backward(dy, cache):
341	    """dy: [B,L,H,P] = dL/dy. Returns dict of grads w.r.t. the scan INPUTS:
342	    dx_h [B,L,H,P], ddt/dA_real/dlam [B,L,H], dtheta [B,L,Nc],
343	    dBbar/dCbar [B,L,Nc,2]. (ddt is grad w.r.t. POST-softplus dt; dlam w.r.t.
344	    lambda=sigmoid(u); dA_real w.r.t. the post-softplus-negated real part.)"""
345	    x_h, dt = cache["x_h"], cache["dt"]
346	    A_real, theta, lam = cache["A_real"], cache["theta"], cache["lam"]
347	    Bbar, Cbar = cache["Bbar"], cache["Cbar"]
348	    alpha, beta, gamma = cache["alpha"], cache["beta"], cache["gamma"]
349	    cos, sin = cache["cos"], cache["sin"]
350	    h_hist, v_hist = cache["h_hist"], cache["v_hist"]
351	    H, P, Nc = cache["H"], cache["P"], cache["Nc"]
352	    B, L, _, _ = x_h.shape
353	    dev, dtp = x_h.device, x_h.dtype
354	
355	    dx_h = torch.zeros_like(x_h)
356	    dalpha = torch.zeros_like(alpha)
357	    dbeta = torch.zeros_like(beta)
358	    dgamma = torch.zeros_like(gamma)
359	    dphi = torch.zeros(B, L, H, Nc, dtype=dtp, device=dev)
360	    dBbar = torch.zeros_like(Bbar)
361	    dCbar = torch.zeros_like(Cbar)
362	
363	    gh = torch.zeros(B, H, P, Nc, 2, dtype=dtp, device=dev)   # dL/dh_t
364	    gv = torch.zeros(B, H, P, Nc, 2, dtype=dtp, device=dev)   # dL/dv_t (from t+1 beta)
365	
366	    for t in reversed(range(L)):
367	        h_t = h_hist[t]
368	        v_t = v_hist[t]
369	        h_tm1 = h_hist[t - 1] if t > 0 else torch.zeros_like(h_t)
370	        v_tm1 = v_hist[t - 1] if t > 0 else torch.zeros_like(v_t)
371	        Cbar_t = Cbar[:, t].view(B, 1, 1, Nc, 2)
372	        Bbar_t = Bbar[:, t].view(B, 1, 1, Nc, 2)
373	        cos_t = cos[:, t].view(B, H, 1, Nc)
374	        sin_t = sin[:, t].view(B, H, 1, Nc)
375	        a_t = alpha[:, t].view(B, H, 1, 1, 1)
376	        b_t = beta[:, t].view(B, H, 1, 1, 1)
377	        g_t = gamma[:, t].view(B, H, 1, 1, 1)
378	        dy_t = dy[:, t].view(B, H, P, 1, 1)              # [B,H,P,1,1]
379	
380	        # (1) y_t = sum_{c,d} Cbar_t * h_t  ->  gh, dCbar
381	        gh = gh + Cbar_t * dy_t                          # [B,H,P,Nc,2]
382	        dCbar[:, t] = (h_t * dy_t).sum(dim=(1, 2))       # sum over H,P (shared)
383	
384	        # (2) v_t total grad = gv (from t+1 beta) + gamma_t * gh (gamma at t)
385	        dv_t = gv + g_t * gh                             # [B,H,P,Nc,2]
386	        # v_t = Bbar_t (.) x_t : dx (sum c,d), dBbar (sum b,h,p)
387	        x_t = x_h[:, t].view(B, H, P, 1, 1)
388	        dx_h[:, t] = (dv_t * Bbar_t).sum(dim=(3, 4))     # [B,H,P]
389	        dBbar[:, t] = (dv_t * x_t).sum(dim=(1, 2))       # [B,Nc,2]
390	
391	        # (3) rotated terms: Rh = R_t h_{t-1}, Rv = R_t v_{t-1}
392	        hr, hi = h_tm1[..., 0], h_tm1[..., 1]
393	        Rh = torch.stack((cos_t * hr - sin_t * hi, sin_t * hr + cos_t * hi), -1)
394	        vr, vi = v_tm1[..., 0], v_tm1[..., 1]
395	        Rv = torch.stack((cos_t * vr - sin_t * vi, sin_t * vr + cos_t * vi), -1)
396	        # per-head coefficient grads (sum over p,c,d within head)
397	        dalpha[:, t] = (Rh * gh).sum(dim=(2, 3, 4))      # [B,H]
398	        dbeta[:, t] = (Rv * gh).sum(dim=(2, 3, 4))
399	        dgamma[:, t] = (v_t * gh).sum(dim=(2, 3, 4))
400	        # phi grad via R'(phi)=[[-sin,-cos],[cos,-sin]] on h_{t-1} (coef alpha)
401	        # and v_{t-1} (coef beta). For coef*R@w with adjoint g=(g0,g1):
402	        #   dphi += coef*( g0*(-sin*w0 - cos*w1) + g1*(cos*w0 - sin*w1) )
403	        g0, g1 = gh[..., 0], gh[..., 1]                  # [B,H,P,Nc]
404	        dRh = g0 * (-sin_t * hr - cos_t * hi) + g1 * (cos_t * hr - sin_t * hi)
405	        dRv = g0 * (-sin_t * vr - cos_t * vi) + g1 * (cos_t * vr - sin_t * vi)
406	        a2 = alpha[:, t].view(B, H, 1, 1)
407	        b2 = beta[:, t].view(B, H, 1, 1)
408	        dphi[:, t] = (a2 * dRh + b2 * dRv).sum(dim=2)    # sum over P -> [B,H,Nc]
409	
410	        # (4) propagate to previous step (R^T adjoint; R^T(phi)=R(-phi))
411	        #   R^T @ g = (cos*g0 + sin*g1, -sin*g0 + cos*g1)
412	        RTg = torch.stack((cos_t * g0 + sin_t * g1,
413	                           -sin_t * g0 + cos_t * g1), -1)  # [B,H,P,Nc,2]
414	        gv = b_t * RTg                                   # dL/dv_{t-1} (beta term)
415	        gh = a_t * RTg                                   # dL/dh_{t-1}
416	
417	    # ---- fold the per-head coefficient Jacobians ----
418	    # alpha=exp(dt*A): dalpha/d(dt)=A*alpha, dalpha/dA=dt*alpha.
419	    # beta=(1-lam)*dt*alpha: dbeta/d(dt)=(1-lam)*alpha*(1+dt*A),
420	    #                        dbeta/dlam=-dt*alpha, dbeta/dA=(1-lam)*dt^2*alpha.
421	    # gamma=lam*dt: dgamma/d(dt)=lam, dgamma/dlam=dt.
422	    # phi=dt*theta: dphi/d(dt)=theta (sum c), dphi/dtheta=dt (sum h).
423	    dt_phi = (dphi * theta.unsqueeze(-2)).sum(dim=-1)    # [B,L,H]
424	    ddt = (dalpha * (A_real * alpha)
425	           + dbeta * ((1.0 - lam) * alpha * (1.0 + dt * A_real))
426	           + dgamma * lam
427	           + dt_phi)                                     # [B,L,H] (post-softplus)
428	    dlam = dbeta * (-dt * alpha) + dgamma * dt           # [B,L,H] (w.r.t. lambda)
429	    dA_real = dalpha * (dt * alpha) + dbeta * ((1.0 - lam) * dt * dt * alpha)
430	    dtheta = (dphi * dt.unsqueeze(-1)).sum(dim=2)        # [B,L,Nc] (sum over H)
431	
432	    return dict(dx_h=dx_h, ddt=ddt, dlam=dlam, dA_real=dA_real,
433	                dtheta=dtheta, dBbar=dBbar, dCbar=dCbar)
434

437	#  ONE Mamba3Layer forward + MANUAL backward, reading the live module's params.
438	#  Param order mirrors named_parameters(): A_log, D, B_bias, Bhat_bias, C_bias,
439	#  Chat_bias, in_proj.w, x_proj.w, dt_proj.w, dt_proj.b, B_norm.w, Bhat_norm.w,
440	#  C_norm.w, Chat_norm.w, out_proj.w  (own params first, then submodules).
441	# ===========================================================================
